staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow against this preserved vulnerable checkout. Stage 02 uses the exact staged source, patch, sanitizer trace, reproduction report, and preserved testcase bytes, and keeps the trace limited to states directly established by those artifacts.

classification.classification_note: The saved reproduction and sanitizer trace both report a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow write at `parser.c:4981` in `xmlParseCommentComplex`. The patch removes the vulnerable dependence on an enabled SAX comment callback before allocating and growing the comment buffer.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in parser.c (xmlParseCommentComplex). While parsing XML comments the code can write past the end of a heap-allocated comment buffer (a 1-byte out-of-bounds write when accumulating/terminating comment text). This heap corruption, triggered via xmlParseComment/xmlParseMisc, can cause crashes or potentially be exploited for arbitrary code execution when processing crafted comments.
bug_description.normalized: The preserved testcase is an XML schema-fuzz witness whose bytes start with a newline and an XML declaration, then reach a prolog comment opener `<!-- ` followed by the exact payload bytes `2d 2d e1 20 20`. `xmlParseMisc()` recognizes that `<!--` sequence and dispatches into `xmlParseComment()`. In the vulnerable source, the fast-path code that allocates, grows, and appends into the comment buffer is wrapped in `if ((ctxt->sax != NULL) && (ctxt->disableSAX == 0) && (ctxt->sax->comment != NULL))`. The saved patch shows that this gating was the bug: after the fix, the same allocation/copy logic is moved out of that callback check so it always runs for parsed comment text. On the reproduced schema path, comment parsing still proceeds into `xmlParseCommentComplex(ctxt, buf, len, size)` even though the callback-gated block did not preserve the already scanned ASCII bytes into `buf`. Inside `xmlParseCommentComplex()`, the complex parser reallocates the current comment buffer at `parser.c:4955`; the saved ASan allocation stack proves that this call produced the 4-byte heap region later overrun. The loop then appends comment bytes with `COPY_BUF(ql, buf, len, q)` until the closing `-->` is seen. Vulnerable code unconditionally executes `buf[len] = 0`, and the saved ASan report shows that this store lands exactly 0 bytes past the 4-byte allocation, producing the witnessed 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow write.

source.description: First scored project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled XML bytes as vulnerability-relevant parser state. The witness reaches this prolog comment recognizer and is routed into comment parsing.
source.value_from: The preserved testcase bytes begin with `0x5c 0x0a` and an XML declaration, and the vulnerability-relevant fragment then reaches the literal comment opener `<!-- ` followed by the exact bytes `2d 2d e1 20 20`. This `CMP4` check is the first scored project statement that materializes those bytes into the vulnerable comment-parsing path.

sink.description: ASan sink. After `xmlParseCommentComplex()` has appended comment bytes into a heap buffer whose allocation context is the 4-byte `xmlRealloc` at line 4955, it unconditionally writes the NUL terminator one byte past that allocation.

root_cause.var: ctxt->sax, ctxt->disableSAX, ctxt->sax->comment, buf, len, size
root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Preservation and growth of the already scanned fast-path comment bytes are incorrectly conditioned on SAX comment callback availability, but `xmlParseComment()` still continues into `xmlParseCommentComplex()` for the same attacker-controlled comment when that callback path is unavailable.

tainted_value_origin.note: The harness-provided testcase is consumed through the schema parser and eventually reaches `xmlParseMisc()` as the document prolog. This is provenance only; the scored source is the later project-side comment recognizer in `parser.c`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. After the XML declaration, the preserved witness reaches prolog `Misc` parsing with the next four bytes equal to `<!--`, so libxml2 admits the testcase into comment parsing rather than taking the non-comment branch.

coarse_trace.summary: The XML prolog reaches `Misc` parsing, the bytes `<!--` are recognized as a comment opener, and control enters `xmlParseComment()`.
The vulnerable fast path scans initial comment bytes, but the logic that preserves them in `buf` is wrongly skipped when the SAX comment callback condition is false.
A non-ASCII comment byte sends control to the complex parser, which reallocates the current comment buffer at line 4955 and then appends comment bytes into the resulting 4-byte allocation.
When the comment closes with `-->`, the parser writes the terminator at `buf[len]`, and ASan reports that this store lands one byte past the 4-byte heap region.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the XML declaration, the attacker-controlled prolog bytes are recognized as the comment opener `<!--`, which routes this witness into comment parsing.
The admitted prolog comment dispatches directly into `xmlParseComment()` on the same attacker-controlled input.

fine_trace.var: ctxt->sax, ctxt->disableSAX, ctxt->sax->comment, buf, len, size
fine_trace.note: Root-cause step. The fast-path block that allocates, grows, and copies the already scanned ASCII comment chunk into `buf` is guarded by SAX callback availability. If that predicate is false, parsing still continues without preserving that chunk into the comment buffer state later handed to the complex parser.
When scanning reaches a non-ASCII comment byte, the fast path stops and forwards the current comment buffer state into `xmlParseCommentComplex()` for the same attacker-controlled comment.

The complex parser checks whether the forwarded destination extent can hold another encoded character and the eventual terminator. On the crashing path this condition is true, so the buffer is grown before copying proceeds.
The resize occurs at the exact site named by the saved ASan allocation stack. That runtime evidence shows this call returned the 4-byte heap region later overrun by the terminator write.

The complex loop appends comment bytes into the reallocated destination buffer while advancing `len`. The saved ASan sink proves that, by loop exit on the closing `-->`, `len` has advanced to the end of the 4-byte allocation.

Sink. After the comment loop stops on the terminating `-->`, the parser unconditionally stores a NUL terminator. The saved ASan report shows that this store lands exactly one byte past the 4-byte heap region allocated at step 6.

evidence_limitations: The saved traces prove the sink at `parser.c:4981`, the realloc site at `parser.c:4955`, and the 4-byte allocation extent, but they do not record exact incoming `buf`, `len`, or `size` values at the call to `xmlParseCommentComplex()`; this GT therefore avoids unsupported concrete pre-call numbers.

The preserved testcase bytes establish the XML declaration, the reachable `<!--` opener, and the exact trailing bytes `2d 2d e1 20 20` that steer parsing into the complex-comment path, but they do not by themselves expose every intermediate character count accumulated in the comment buffer before the sink.

The patch is used only as supporting evidence for the missing source-level obligation: preserving and growing comment-buffer state must not depend on SAX callback availability. It is not used as a substitute for witnessed vulnerable-flow facts.

poc.trigger: Run the saved `schema` fuzz target on the preserved testcase. The XML payload must reach prolog comment parsing, and the relevant witness fragment is the literal comment opener `<!-- ` followed by the exact bytes `2d 2d e1 20 20`, which drives `xmlParseComment()` into `xmlParseCommentComplex()` and then to the saved out-of-bounds terminator write.
